description: The figure presents three separate pie charts summarizing the distribution of quantifier/operation categories for (1) Categorical reasoning, (2) Approximate Number Generation, and (3) Disjunctive vs. Conjunctive reasoning, with each slice labeled directly with its percentage and no separate legend. The Categorical pie chart contains 4 slices: “Universal Quantifiers” in a very light blue/gray at 29.07%, “Limiter” in pale pink at 27.91%, “Negation” in light peach/orange at 27.91%, and “Existential Quantifiers” in pale green at 15.12%; the labels and percentages are printed inside the slices, and no slice is exploded or otherwise emphasized. The Approximate Number Generation pie chart contains 3 slices: “Approximate Quantities” in pale cream/yellow at 45.03%, “Comparative Relationships” in light blue at 36.26%, and “Absolute Absence” in light lavender at 18.71%, again with internal labels and no visual emphasis. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive pie chart contains 2 slices: “Disjunctive” in very light bluish gray at 49.51% and “Conjunctive” in pale mauve/pink at 50.49%, with the two halves appearing nearly equal and labeled inside; across all three charts, the segment ordering appears to follow the circular layout rather than an explicitly indicated sorted order.
